title: 22-layer ZnS/Al2O3 alternating stack with independent thickness optimization on CaF2
scientific_hypothesis: An alternating high/low index dielectric stack with 22 layers can produce two distinct transmission windows at 3.25-3.35 μm and 4.20-4.30 μm through constructive interference, while adjacent bands experience destructive interference and suppression.
design_principle: Quarter-wave stack theory: alternating layers with optical thickness near λ/4 create high reflectance stopbands. By deviating from strict quarter-wave thicknesses and optimizing individually, multiple passbands can emerge at specific wavelengths where phase conditions allow transmission. The index contrast between ZnS and Al2O3 provides sufficient reflectance per interface to build effective stopbands with ~11 layer pairs.
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 3.25-3.35 μm band
Maximize mean transmittance in 4.20-4.30 μm band
Minimize mean transmittance in 2.50-3.10 μm band
Minimize mean transmittance in 4.45-5.00 μm band
manufacturing_considerations: 22 layers is within stated limit of 24
ZnS and Al2O3 are conventional evaporatable/sputterable IR dielectrics
Total thickness ~15-20 μm may require stress management
theory_basis: Recalled: ZnS has refractive index ~2.2-2.4 in 3-5 μm range with low extinction
Recalled: Al2O3 has refractive index ~1.6-1.7 in mid-IR with good transparency
Recalled: Quarter-wave stacks produce stopbands centered at design wavelength
Recalled: Deviating from quarter-wave thickness can create multiple passbands
Recalled: CaF2 (Daimon-20 dataset) is transparent in 2.5-5.0 μm range and commonly used as IR substrate
expected_advantages: High index contrast (~0.5-0.7) provides strong interference effects per layer pair
22 layers gives ~11 pairs, sufficient for deep stopbands
Independent thickness optimization allows tuning for dual-band requirement
All materials are conventional IR coating materials
known_risks: Uncertain: Exact n/k dispersion of ZnS and Al2O3 across 2.5-5.0 μm - need registry data to confirm
Uncertain: Whether Al2O3 has absorption features in 4-5 μm range that would limit performance
Uncertain: Daimon-20 CaF2 substrate refractive index at these wavelengths affects matching
Uncertain: Whether 22 layers is optimal or if fewer layers could achieve similar performance
Uncertain: Deposition stress and adhesion for thick multi-layer stacks not verified
What would settle: Measured dispersion data from registry, stress measurements from deposition trials
execution_request_english: Optimize a 22-layer planar multilayer coating on CaF2 (Daimon-20) substrate with air incidence. Stack sequence: ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat), ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat), ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat), ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat), ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat), ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat), ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat), ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat), ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat), ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat), ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat) (22 coating layers total). Optimize all 22 layer thicknesses independently with bounds ±25 nm around baseline [911.21, 804.98, 703.61, 672.14, 356.02, 1229.24, 356.71, 570.30, 870.84, 635.33, 370.60, 1162.40, 332.44, 462.47, 857.27, 417.97, 831.12, 1275.13, 925.63, 416.00, 805.81, 889.71] nm. Target: maximize transmittance in 3250-3350 nm and 4200-4300 nm bands, minimize transmittance in 2500-3100 nm and 4450-5000 nm bands. Use coherent transfer matrix method. Materials: zns, Al2O3 (Kischkat), substrate CaF2 (Daimon-20). No metal layers. Layer count fixed at 22.
revision_reason: Continuation from iteration_19: Relax thickness optimization bounds from ±15 nm to ±25 nm around best candidate from round 4 (thicknesses: [911.21, 804.98, 703.61, 672.14, 356.02, 1229.24, 356.71, 570.30, 870.84, 635.33, 370.60, 1162.40, 332.44, 462.47, 857.27, 417.97, 831.12, 1275.13, 925.63, 416.00, 805.81, 889.71] nm). This widens phase-tuning bandwidth while anchoring near proven geometry. Repaired material name from CaF2 to Daimon-20 per registry resolution requirement.
